text.p: Schering-Plough Corp and Myriad Genetics Inc said Wednesday they had begun a strategic alliance to discover genes and develop therapies for prostate and other cancers.
The deal brings together Myriad's gene discovery and protein interaction expertise and Schering Plough's experience in developing and marketing cancer treatments, they said.
Myriad will retain exclusive rights to all diagnostic products and services and will receive royalties on all pharmaceutical products developed by Schering-Plough from genes discovered by Myriad.

The agreement covers three years of research, extendable to five years. Assuming the full five years, and the full development of five target genes, payments to Myriad -- excluding royalties -- would be $60 million, the companies said.

"This agreement is consistent with our strategy to establish partnership with leading pharmaceutical companies to develop therapies based on our gene discoveries,' said Peter Meldrum, chief executive and chairman of Myriad.

"While this research program is targeted primarily at discovering new prostate cancer therapies, it is likely to have a broader application to other cancers as well," said Cecil Pickett, executive vice president of discovery research at Schering-Plough.
Myriad shares were 1-1/2 higher at 24-1/4, Schering-Plough was was down 3/8 at 76-5/8.
